skill.name: generate-api-client
skill.description: Generates a type-safe API client from an OpenAPI api-docs.yaml file using Orval, then checks generated TypeScript output.
skill.summary: Generate Orval API clients from OpenAPI specifications and verify generated TypeScript types.
skill.author: Crearize

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives caused by markdown code fences and read-only ls examples. Two command blocks are confirmed medium-risk because they run pnpm and npx project tooling in a community repository. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or hidden authority claims were found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Before running pnpm run generate:api, inspect package.json and the lockfile, then request user confirmation in untrusted repositories.
Prefer a trusted local TypeScript binary through the project package manager and avoid package downloads during generation.
State that commands should run only after the user confirms the project path, dependencies, and OpenAPI specification source.

content.value_statement: Manual API client updates drift when OpenAPI contracts change. This skill guides Orval generation and type checking so frontend clients stay aligned.
actual_capabilities: Runs the frontend Orval generation script through the project package manager.
Verifies generated API client files under frontend/src/lib/api/generated.
Runs TypeScript type checking after client generation.
Produces a concise completion report with generated file names and next steps.
limitations: Assumes the OpenAPI file is named api-docs.yaml at the documented backend path.
Assumes the frontend project already defines a generate:api script.
Does not create or repair the Orval configuration.
Does not validate API behavior beyond TypeScript compilation.

use_cases.description: Regenerate the TypeScript API client after the OpenAPI contract changes, then confirm the generated files and types.

use_cases.title: Keep full-stack contracts aligned

use_cases.title: Standardize generated client reviews
use_cases.description: Apply a repeatable checklist for API client generation before merging contract or frontend integration changes.

prompt_templates.title: Generate from the current spec

prompt_templates.prompt: Use generate-api-client to confirm the OpenAPI file exists, run the configured Orval generation, and report the generated files.

output_examples.input: Generate the frontend client from the current OpenAPI spec.
output_examples.output: The skill confirms the spec path, runs Orval, checks generated API and model files, and reports type-check status.

output_examples.input: Regenerate the API client after a backend endpoint changed.
output_examples.output: The skill updates the generated client from the latest contract and summarizes whether TypeScript validation passed.

output_examples.input: Find out why API client generation is failing.
output_examples.output: The skill separates spec lookup, generation, file verification, and type checking so the failing phase is clear.

best_practices: Review OpenAPI changes before regenerating the client.
Inspect project package scripts before running generation in an untrusted repository.
Commit generated client changes with the related backend contract change when the repository expects generated files.
anti_patterns: Editing generated API client files by hand instead of changing the OpenAPI spec or Orval configuration.
Running generation before dependencies and package scripts are reviewed.

faq.question: Does this skill require Orval?
faq.answer: Yes. It assumes the project already has Orval configured and exposes generation through a frontend package script.

faq.question: Where does it expect the OpenAPI file?
faq.answer: It checks backend/src/main/resources/static/api-docs.yaml before running the generation flow.

faq.question: Does it create the Orval configuration?
faq.answer: No. It uses the existing project configuration and focuses on running and verifying generation.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it call external services?
faq.answer: No evidence found in SKILL.md. The documented flow uses local project commands and local files.

faq.question: What should I check before running it?
faq.answer: Review package scripts, dependencies, and the OpenAPI source when working in a community or untrusted repository.
